draft.title: Flat-rate depreciation
card: Depreciation is the fall in an asset's value over time. With flat-rate depreciation, the asset loses the same dollar amount each period.
The rule is V(n+1) = V(n) − d, where V(0) is the starting value and d is the amount lost each period. The value after n periods is V(n) = V(0) − d × n.
The graph of value against time is a straight line going down. The gradient is −d.
Example: a $12 000 printer loses $1500 each year. After 4 years, V(4) = 12 000 − 1500 × 4 = $6000.
draft.remember: Flat-rate depreciation takes off the same dollar amount every period, so the value falls in a straight line.

a.q: A machine is bought for $20 000 and loses $2500 in value each year. What is its value after 3 years?
a.why: V(3) = 20 000 − 2500 × 3 = 20 000 − 7500 = $12 500. The value $17 500 is only the value after 1 year, because the loss was taken off once instead of three times.
a.clue: Take the yearly loss off once for each year.

b.q: Mia's café buys an oven for $9000. After 5 years its value is $4000 using flat-rate depreciation. How much value does it lose each year?
b.why: The total loss is 9000 − 4000 = $5000 over 5 years. So d = 5000 ÷ 5 = $1000 a year. The value $5000 is the total loss, not the loss for one year.
b.clue: Find the total fall in value, then share it across the years.

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers check out ($20 000 − 3 × $2500 = $12 500; $5000 ÷ 5 = $1000), the card's rule, graph and example are correct, and the distractors reflect sensible errors.
